Within the week, a modest sum went south from the House's general almsfund, the kind Aethelgard's stewards disbursed to flood-hit tenants and townsfolk up and down the river every few years without any particular fuss, addressed to no one in Duskmere by name and drawing on no line of the ledger that could be traced back to any single request.

He could have had the whole of that riverbank rebuilt in an afternoon and never broken a sweat doing it — could have gone south himself and set new stone in place with his own hands faster than any crew of masons Duskmere could hire in a season — and he told me the wanting to do exactly that was almost impossible to sit still against.

Gives Draconis real personal texture for the first time in the series — a concrete hometown (Duskmere) and sibling (Halyn) — per the brief's explicit instruction, deepening CC-085's relationship beyond guard-and-ward into two people who know each other as people.

...ould be the last time he meant to tell it to me, that he had come to think of that whole stretch of years — the road and the wine and the beam, the guardhouse and the coastal command, the letter from Duskmere and the lake and the border bolt, all of it — as one long conversation the two of them had been having without either ever once speaking its true subject aloud....

He told him everything, once he started — Duskmere's narrow streets and its smell of river reed, his mother's grave there, the four siblings the current had taken in four different directions over the years, and Halyn, who by his account had always been the steadiest of them and now had nothing steady left under her at all.

...Draconis told him about Duskmere again, not the letter and the flood this time but the ordinary childhood underneath it — a brother who'd once fallen through river ice and come up laughing before anyone had finished being frightened for him, a mother who could gut a fish faster than any of her five children ever managed to learn, a whole small unremarkable life lived long before any of it had anything to do with Hous...

Introduces two new minor named figures, both one-scene and off-page: Draconis's younger sister Halyn, and his hometown, the river town of Duskmere — both grepped against the full live ledger before drafting and collision-checked clean.
